insurer: HDFC ERGO General Insurance Company Limited
sumInsured: Individual: 1L to 50L (by variant). Family Floater: 2L to 50L (by variant).

great.name: No Claim Bonus
great.quote: “On Renewal of this Policy with the Company without a break, a sum equal to 10% of the Base Sum Insured of the expiring Policy shall be provided as multiplier benefit irrespective of any claims... The maximum multiplier bonus will not exceed 100% of the Basic Sum Insured in any Policy Year.”
great.explanation: A 10% multiplier benefit is added on renewal even if you make claims, up to a maximum of 100% of the Base Sum Insured. This means your cover can grow up to double over time without being reduced just because you claimed.

great.name: Co-pay
great.quote: “Co-payment means a cost-sharing requirement... the policyholder/insured will bear a specified percentage of the admissible claim amount.”
great.explanation: Only a glossary definition of co-payment is provided and no applied co-pay clause is stated in the extracted text. This indicates no co-pay is charged on the plan, so the insurer should pay 100% of admissible claims.

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: “30-day waiting period... Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the first policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident”
good.explanation: Illnesses are not covered for the first 30 days from the policy start date, except for accidents. This is a standard market waiting period and mainly affects claims soon after buying the policy.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting
good.quote: “Specified disease/procedure waiting period... excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with us.”
good.explanation: Listed specified diseases/procedures are not covered until you complete 24 months of continuous coverage. This is a common 2-year wait and can delay claims for those listed conditions.

good.name: PED Waiting Period
good.quote: “Expenses related to the treatment of a pre-existing disease (PED) and its direct complications shall be excluded until the expiry of 36 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with insurer.”
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases and their direct complications are covered only after 36 months of continuous coverage. This 3-year waiting period is common in retail health insurance and matters most if you already have known conditions.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: “Pre-Hospitalization Medical Expenses... incurred upto 60 days before the date of admission to the Hospital”
good.explanation: Medical expenses incurred up to 60 days before hospital admission are covered if they relate to the hospitalization. This helps pay for consultations, tests, and medicines leading up to admission.

good.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: “Post-Hospitalization Medical Expenses... incurred upto 90 days after discharge from Hospitalisation”
good.explanation: Medical expenses incurred up to 90 days after discharge are covered if they relate to the hospitalization. This supports follow-up care like medicines, diagnostics, and doctor visits after you go home.

bad.name: Restore Benefit
bad.quote: No clause found in provided wording for restoration/reinstatement/reload of Sum Insured after a claim.
bad.reference: Not mentioned in the provided sections
bad.explanation: No restoration/reinstatement of Sum Insured is mentioned in the provided wording. This means once the Sum Insured is used up in a policy year, further claims in the same year may not be payable.

bad.name: Consumables
bad.quote: “Annexure I - List I - Items for which coverage is not available in the policy” (includes) “GLOVES”, “MASK”, “NEBULISATION KIT”, “ANY KIT WITH NO DETAILS MENTIONED [DELIVERY KIT, ORTHOKIT, RECOVERY KIT, ETC]”
bad.explanation: Common consumables like gloves, masks, nebulisation kits and various procedure kits are listed as not covered. This increases out-of-pocket costs during hospitalization because hospitals routinely bill these items.

unclear.name: Room Rent
unclear.quote: “Room Rent means the amount charged by a hospital towards room and boarding expenses and shall include associated medical expenses.”
unclear.explanation: Only a definition of room rent is provided and no eligible room category or cap is stated in the extracted text. Your actual room eligibility (and whether proportionate deductions can apply) would depend on the schedule/benefit table.
